findings.issue: Each of the 15 GetErrorCode arms ends with 'if 2 == _param1: return _param2', which is dead there (uint24(_param1) is 1 or 10..20), followed by a memory-built Error(string), a shared copy loop and a raw revert: about 200 lines for a 3-line function. findings.rule: x == c implies uint24(x) == c mod 2^24, so in a branch where uint24(x) == k != 2 the test x == 2 is false: fold it. The revert data of each arm are then constants, printed as revert with '<string>'; the function becomes 'if x == 2: return _param2' plus the per-code reverts.

findings.source: TuringHelper.sol:143-145 bytes memory response = Self.GetResponse(1, _url, _payload); emit OffchainResponse(0x01, response); return response; (127 with rType 0x02000001)
findings.issue: The string and bytes arguments are printed as raw ABI words (offsets 96 and ceil32(len) + 128, the first length, then one memory slice holding the rest), the returned bytes is decoded with a copy loop (P7), and the event and the return show the raw (offset, length, data) layout instead of the bytes value.
findings.rule: When head words are offsets to [len, data] blocks of the same buffer, print each as Array(len, data) (here _url[all], _payload[all]); a return or event field encoded as (offset, len, data) is Array(len, data), and a copy loop whose source is the decoded bytes is that value.

notes: Boba TuringHelper (solc 0.8.9). No explicit loop in the source; the 5 whiles are implicit copies (P7): the Error(string) data in Get42, GetRandom and GetResponse, and abi.decode of the returned bytes in TuringTx/TuringTxV2. All 15 ABI functions and the fallback (plain revert) read in full against TuringHelper.sol and Ownable: onlyOwner/onlyPermittedCaller checks, storage writes (permittedCaller as stor2, Self as stor1), events (printed by topic hash, names absent from the database), Self.Get42(2, 42) / GetRandom(1, 0) / GetResponse(1 or 0x02000001, ...) calls with bubbled reverts, GetErrorCode's 0x00ffffff mask (uint24 tests) and its evaluation before the rType == 2 test (require evaluates its message first). The Error(string) offsets and lengths in Get42/GetRandom (68 + ceil32(L)) are exact. GetResponse's last two codes (20, unknown) still share one memory-built revert. The diff from the round-1 text shows only improvements: whole-byte hex, GetResponse returns Array(len, data), the event/return copy loops of TuringTx folded, and the GetResponse call arguments no longer mis-decoded (the old text printed one Array spanning both strings). P11/P12: the 30 dead 'if 2 == _param1' tests and their duplicated revert setup.
summary: Faithful, loop-free contract; readability suffers in Get42/GetRandom (15 arms with dead returns and memory-built reverts where GetResponse shows direct reverts) and in TuringTx/V2, whose string/bytes call arguments, return and event stay in raw ABI form.
